title: Tiered ejection and soft rehome for edge sessions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: In active-active edge deployments we observe simultaneous small-region degradations that cause abrupt eviction of in-flight streaming sessions and high client-side error spikes. Current failover is either all-or-nothing (full drain + cutover) or naive sticky-routing that causes long tails. Goal: implement a tiered ejection policy with a 'soft rehome' handshake for streaming and sessionful requests so traffic is migrated with minimal dropped frames and predictable latency impact while preserving SLOs. This ticket covers design, implementation, rollout plan, and monitoring for the feature.
acceptance_criteria: New tiered-ejection policy can evict up to 30% of regional capacity gracefully by priority class without violating 99th percentile latency SLO by more than 10%
Streaming sessions (WebSocket/HTTP-stream) experience less than 1% dropped-stream errors during a region-level partial ejection test
Session affinity is preserved for high-priority tokens using a grace-window and token watermarking mechanism
Automated rollback via feature flag and circuit breaker returns system to baseline within 60s when adverse regressions are detected
Documentation and runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and PM
End-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios added to canary pipeline
design_notes: We will introduce three contract changes: (1) tiered ejection controller that grades backends by health and telemetry and evicts according to 'priority buckets' (critical, standard, best-effort); (2) soft-rehome handshake for session/streaming tokens that attempts in-band resume using a short-lived rehome token and KV-forwarding for small KV cache state; (3) circuit-breaker layer with staged thresholds that trigger selective load-shedding for best-effort traffic before impacting critical tokens. The handshake uses a 'rehome_v1' header that contains a rehome_token and target-region hint; if the target accepts, it performs a delta KV fetch for keys listed in the token to warm caches and continues the stream with a 200-ok resume. If the handshake fails, the origin will attempt a retry to another region within the priority bucket. Metric-driven thresholds: start soft ejection when p95 latency >150ms *and* server_error_rate >0.5% for 5m; escalate to hard ejection if p99 latency >600ms or server_error_rate >3% sustained for 2m. Load-shedding strategy: best-effort gets randomized 30-60% shed at first tier, standard gets queue-limited and CPU-backed batching reduced by 20%, critical is never shed unless catastrophic load and then at most 5% randomized sample to maintain core SLOs.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Prototype soft-rehome handshake in staging (Luca + SRE) - implement header format and ephemeral rehome tokens (2w)
Phase B: Implement tiered-ejection controller and expose policy via routing-config (3w)
Phase C: Integrate circuit-breaker staged thresholds and load-shedding hooks into gateway routing loop (2w)
Phase D: Add canary pipeline tests and chaos recipes (chaos monkey: delay/drop, partial region partition) (1w)
Phase E: Gradual rollout behind feature flag: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics gates and rollback criteria (2w)
Phase F: Post-rollout hardening and docs (1w)
rollout_plan: Enable feature-flag=edge.soft_rehome in staging and run full regression tests
Canary deploy to eu-west-1 with 1% of edge traffic, observe p95/p99 latency and streaming error rates for 48h
If stable, increase to 5% and run synthetic stream-heavy workloads, verify dropped-stream <1%
Expand to 20% and run short chaos experiment (simulate node loss) to validate resume paths
Only after two successful 48h windows across different regions move to 50% and then full rollout
Provide a quick rollback toggle and a kill-switch circuit-breaker that signs all new rehome tokens as disabled
testing_plan: Unit tests for rehome token generation/validation and KV-list serialization
Integration test: origin+target handshake flow with simulated partial KV warmup (CI)
Load test: 200k RPS mixed text generation + 10k concurrent streams with controlled tail latency injections
Chaos test: region partial partition + 30% node termination while soft_rehome is active
SLO regression test: synthetic traffic ensures p99 does not regress beyond acceptance thresholds
monitoring: New Grafana dashboard: Edge Soft-Rehome Overview (metrics: rehome_attempts, rehome_success_rate, rehome_latency_ms_p95/p99, per-priority dropped_stream_rate)
Alerts: rehome_success_rate < 95% for 5m => P1; dropped_stream_rate > 1% for critical for 5m => Pager
SLO budget burn rate monitors integrated with Opsgenie: if burn rate >3x in 1h, auto-pause rollout
Telemetry: log rehome decisions, target selection reason, and KV keys requested (masked) for auditing
Dashboards for circuit-breaker trips and load-shedding percentages per region and per priority
